subject: Order Form SLA: maintenance lanes, uptime bracketing & credit calculation
messages:
From: Devon Price <devon.price@auroracorp.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@auroracorp.com
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarify uptime measurement + maintenance lane proposal

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Procurement asked me to capture two open items on the SLA side before we move the Order Form to signatures:

1) How you measure uptime for multi-region deployments (do you use aggregated across regions or per-region measurement?)
2) Proposal for planned maintenance: procurement expects advance notice and wants a clear "maintenance lane" definition so that scheduled work doesn't count against uptime. They also want the credit formula in a worked example.

Attached is a one-page from our side with expectations (our procurement prefers 99.99% baseline, 30-day UTC measurement, and 72-hour notice for >30m windows). Can you confirm Redwood's tolerance and suggest language we can include in the OF?

Also copying Aurora contracts for visibility.

Thanks,
Devon
Devon Price
Head of Procurement, AuroraCorp
Email: devon.price@auroracorp.com
Attachments: aurora-sla-expectations.pdf (stub)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Devon Price <devon.price@auroracorp.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify uptime measurement + maintenance lane proposal

Devon —

Appreciate the note and the example doc. High level response: Redwood measures uptime per contract-defined service boundary (per-region by default unless customer requests global aggregation), and we can add explicit language to define measurement windows and planned maintenance lanes.

Quick summary of proposed changes I asked Legal to redline:
- Define the "measurement period" as UTC calendar month for clarity.
- Measurement is per-service endpoint in the region(s) listed in the Order Form by default; customer can request aggregated reporting as an add-on.
- Planned maintenance is scoped into two "lanes":
  * Routine Patch (SLA-impacting unless scheduled in a booked maintenance slot): customers must be notified 72 hours in advance for windows >30 minutes.
  * Non-Impact Maintenance (configuration/metadata updates, telemetry jobs) — these are excluded from uptime if performed during a pre-agreed weekly window.
- Emergency Patches — attempt to avoid SLA impact, but will be excluded from credit calculations only for verified security hotfixes with post-facto audit logs.
- Service credit tiers: propose a three-tier credit table (>=99.95%: 0; 99.50–99.95%: 10% credit; <99.50%: 25% credit) with a monthly cap of 50% of fees.

I attached a sample redline (Aurora_MSA_redline_v3.docx) and a simple model with examples of how credits would apply (uptime-bracket-model.xlsx). Laura — see the redline in section 3.1 and the proposed credit table; happy to take sharper legal language if you want to replace bullets with clause text.

Next steps I recommend: Laura provides line edits for the MSA/Order Form language; Marcus confirm that the operational approach (72-hour notice, per-region) matches what Sales promised in the SOW; Devon, we can then put the redline back to Aurora for a single pass.

Action items:
- Laura: provide legal clause text by EOD tomorrow (Fri 10 Jul).
- Marcus: confirm operations/CS can commit to the 72-hour notice and weekly non-impact windows.
- Devon: flag any hard stops to your procurement team.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Security & Compliance (acting for contract reviews)
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Aurora_MSA_redline_v3.docx (redline stub), uptime-bracket-model.xlsx (stub)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, devon.price@auroracorp.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify uptime measurement + maintenance lane proposal

Hi all,

Thanks Irene — I took a pass on the MSA redline and have two main legal suggestions to keep the language tight and limit open-ended exposure:

1) Measurement window & aggregation:
- Propose clause: "Uptime shall be measured on a per-Order-Form service endpoint basis over the UTC calendar month. Customer may request aggregated cross-region reporting; aggregation does not change the baseline uptime calculation unless expressly specified in the Order Form."

2) Planned maintenance & exclusions:
- Propose clause: "Planned Maintenance" means maintenance scheduled at least seventy-two (72) hours in advance by mutual agreement. Planned Maintenance windows up to sixty (60) minutes per occurrence are excluded from uptime calculations when scheduled within the agreed maintenance lane; occurrences exceeding sixty (60) minutes require explicit acceptance from Customer or will be counted against uptime unless otherwise agreed in writing.
- We should avoid an open-ended emergency carveout. Limit emergency exclusion to documented security hotfixes where Redwood provides post-event audit evidence within five (5) business days.

3) Service credits and caps:
- Replace the informal table Irene suggested with a short clause and attach the credit table as an Order Form schedule. Key legal points: cap credits at 50% of monthly fees; credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for uptime failures; fees are not refundable.

I've attached a redline with clause text (section numbers and suggested definitions updated). Devon — this follows industry norms and keeps exposure predictable. If Aurora absolutely requires 99.99% we need to discuss either an SLA-backed premium or else narrow the measurement scope (e.g., only for a single region or a limited set of endpoints).

Next: Marcus / Ops - can you confirm whether the engineering team can guarantee 72-hour notice and maintain a weekly non-impact window (e.g., Sundays 02:00–04:00 UTC) that we can propose?

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Aurora_MSA_redline_v3_clauses.docx (stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com, devon.price@auroracorp.com
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:32:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify uptime measurement + maintenance lane proposal

All — quick operations confirmation. Engineering and SRE reviewed the proposed lanes. We can commit to:

- 72-hour advance notice for any Planned Maintenance >30 minutes.
- A weekly "non-impact" maintenance window (Sunday 02:00–04:00 UTC) for non-customer-facing telemetry and low-risk infra work; we will exclude work performed in this window from uptime calculations if scheduled and mutually agreed.
- Emergency hotfixes: we will attempt to schedule during a maintenance window when safe to do so; if taken immediately for security reasons, we will provide audit logs and post-mortem within five business days to support exclusion per the contract clause.

On the credit table: Ops prefers a slightly more graduated table to reflect runway: 0 credits >=99.95%; 5% credits 99.8–99.95%; 15% credits 99.0–99.8%; 35% credits <99.0% with monthly cap 50%. I know Laura proposed a simpler 3-tier table; happy to sync on the final numbers if Aurora wants a worked example — I attached an example calculation in uptime-bracket-model.xlsx.

If this works for everyone, Irene / Laura: please send a combined redline we can route to DocuSign once Aurora confirms.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
CC: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachments: planned-maintenance-examples.pdf (stub), uptime-bracket-model.xlsx (updated stub)
